summary: Functional requirements say what the system does — functions turning inputs into outputs, captured in user stories and use cases inside the SRS.
title: Functional requirements

summary: NFRs name the system's qualities — testable characteristics of functions, never functions themselves, with no such thing as a purely non-functional use case.
title: Non-functional requirements: overview

locators: Lecture 4, PDF p. 47 (in-scope vs business rules)
summary: Valid NFRs are unambiguous, doable, verifiable, in-scope and truly non-functional — testable constraints, never disguised functions or vibes.
title: What makes an NFR valid

summary: Performance requirements bind an operation, a time bound, a workload and an environment — then verify with repeated, statistically-ruled measurement.
title: Performance requirements

summary: Reliability is failure behaviour quantified: MTTF/MTBF, availability, POFOD, ROCOF — chosen to fit the usage pattern, bounded short of perfection, scoped to a failure class.
title: Reliability requirements and metrics

summary: Usability requirements quantify what defined users can achieve within what time or effort — system-enabled ability, never user obligations.
title: Usability requirements

summary: Security, interoperability, localisation and accessibility complete the NFR palette — propose the parameter that fits the system's risks, then quantify it.
title: Security, interoperability, localisation, accessibility

summary: Six NFR mark-losers: disguised functions, business rules, unquantified adjectives, mismatched metrics, perfection claims, missing environments.
title: NFRs: common exam mistakes
